chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Yaqoub ibn Shu'ayb from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'If the one in Ihram kills an ostrich,' he said, 'Upon him is a badanah (a mature female camel) from the camels.' I said, 'He kills a wild donkey?' He said, 'Upon him is a badanah.' I said, 'So (what about) a cow?' He said, 'A cow.'

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: A mature female camel used as sacrificial expiation

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for killing an ostrich while in Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'kaffarat al-hayawan' (animal expiation) by drawing a direct analogy between the killed animal and the required sacrifice, as narrated by Imam al-Sadiq (AS). It highlights the juristic reasoning used in Shia fiqh to determine compensation based on the type of game hunted during the sacred state of Ihram, reflecting the practical application of Quranic injunctions on hunting prohibitions.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, altogether from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I said to himasws, ‘The one in Ihraam kills an ostrick’. Heasws said: ‘Upon him is a sacrificial animal from the camels’. I said, ‘He kills a wild donkey’. Heasws said: ‘Upon him is a sacrificial animal’. I said, ‘So (what about if he kills) a cow?’ Heasws said: ‘(Upon him is) a cow’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn all from Safwan ibn Yahya from Ya’qub ibn Shu’ayb who has said the following: “

I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who kills an ostrich. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes one badanah of camel.’ I then asked about wild donkey. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes one badanah.’ I then asked about cow. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes one cow.’”
